gap: No result ChatGPT got puts these two things side by side. First, the 28, 32 and 40 MP figures on the FLEX-M, FLEX-M2 and FLEX-DARK never reach the phone on the free plan, which sends SD previews only. To get HD you need the Standard plan ($7/mo billed annually, 1,000 photos) or a pack at $0.10 per photo, and Hook & Barrel says even Full-HD transmissions are compressed, not the 32 MP originals. Second, the FLEX-M2's spec sheet says 'up to six months' on 8 AA, but Outdoor Life's camera ran out after about 1.5 months. Batteries, not a plan, are the cost that keeps coming back.
standout_why: I compared against the cited SPYPOINT FLEX-M page (it labels the Free plan 'SD Photos' and Standard/Premium 'HD'), the cited 2023 SPYPOINT blog (100 free photos, 28 MP, nothing on transmitted resolution), trailcamspecs.com ('standard-resolution', $5/50 Full-HD, $5/20 video), camandcanopy.com ('downsized', no pixel figures), moultrie.com/plans and Outdoor Life (Moultrie sends every photo in HD, Tactacam charges $5/50 for HD, and the FLEX-M2's AA batteries died after about 1.5 months). The SD-only part is already in rival pages. What they lack: (a) the point that the MP gap between FLEX models buys nothing you see on the phone under the free plan; (b) the claim of 6 months against about 1.5 months measured on the same model; (c) price per photo worked out on the same basis across free, pack and plan. That is partial overlap, not new ground.
decides: This confirms the FLEX-M at $59.99 as the pick for someone who wants it completely free. On the free tier, the extra $20 for the FLEX-M2 ($79.99) or $60 for the FLEX-DARK ($119.99) does not get sharper phone photos, because all three send the same 100 SD previews a month. The extra money buys hardware: the FLEX-DARK lists a 0.3 s trigger against 0.4 s, 100 ft detection against 90 ft, and no-glow flash. The page should tell the shopper two things. Once they want HD on the phone, the cheapest way is Standard annual: $84 a year for 1,000 HD photos a month, against $0.10 per photo in packs. And on AA batteries they should plan on swapping a set of 8 every couple of months, not twice a year.
